business_problem: CarGurus wanted to stop spending engineering time on self-managed databases and disaster-recovery tasks as marketplace data volumes grew, while also accelerating provisioning and reducing database operating costs.
solution_summary: CarGurus moved growing MongoDB workloads from self-managed deployments to MongoDB Atlas on AWS so its engineers could focus on vehicle marketplace features rather than database operations. Atlas now underpins listing and marketplace data services, while MongoDB Time Series Collections stores and analyzes temporal data in the same managed environment. Because provisioning, availability, disaster recovery, and performance tuning are handled by Atlas, developers no longer spend cycles on manual administration; monitoring and right-sizing features help the company control cost as data volumes rise. The migration also streamlined rollout of new environments, replacing weeks-long database setup with provisioning measured in minutes, and gave the database engineering team a simpler path to keep moving the rest of its estate to Atlas.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Hosts CarGurus marketplace databases as a managed service on AWS so engineers avoid manual operations work.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Time Series Collections
solution_components.role: Stores and analyzes temporal marketplace data inside the Atlas deployment.

data_flow: Dealer and marketplace data is stored in MongoDB Atlas on AWS, while time-based operational data is written into MongoDB Time Series Collections for analysis. Atlas then serves application workloads while built-in monitoring and right-sizing guide the ongoing migration and optimization of databases.
business_outcome: Atlas reduced operational overhead, helped developers provision databases in minutes instead of weeks, and improved time to market while giving the CarGurus team better cost visibility and simpler scaling.
